lesson_title: Paper 1 Practice Run: Walking the Exam Question by Question
hook_text: Six questions. You answer FOUR. Here's how the pros pick — and how the marks actually land.
clip_script: Economics Paper 1: six questions, 150 marks — but you only answer four. Question 1 is compulsory: thirty objective marks. One word, two marks: savings, taxes and imports leaving the circular flow are... leakages. Banked. Then Section B: three forty-mark questions, you choose TWO. Open each, look straight at the data — the graph, the table. Can you read this business cycle diagram? Bottom of the dip: trough. Crest: peak. The gap between crest and trend line: amplitude — how hard the economy swings. Four-mark answers are just four number sentences: exports 1 200 plus gold 100 minus imports 1 400 — trade balance minus 100 million. Write the method, label the answer, collect every mark. Then ONE essay from two, and its forty marks are four boxes: define for 2. Develop your headings for 26 — two marks per linked fact. Argue your own judgement for 10. Land one fresh thought for 2. Nothing in this paper asks for genius. It asks for pieces, delivered in order — and after this practice run, you know every piece by name.
visual_style: An exam paper splitting into four glowing chosen questions while two fade grey; a wave diagram with trough, peak and amplitude labels stamping in; number sentences assembling like train carriages; the essay as four boxes filling 2, 26, 10, 2.
pacing: Quick hits through Section A, a measured beat on the data reading, a strong four-count rhythm on the essay boxes.
call_to_action: Do the full practice run and walk into Paper 1 already knowing how every mark lands.
